summary: Customer A is currently classified as High Risk due to multiple early-warning signals, including a significant revenue decline, negative cash flow, collateral devaluation, and contagion risk from a related company. The customer operates in the Seafood industry, which is experiencing a sustained downturn.

findings.statement: Customer A experienced a 20.6% drop in 90-day revenue compared to the baseline average.
The customer has recorded negative net cash flow for two consecutive periods (-633.2 and -855.3).
Related company An Phat Garment Co. is currently 17 days past due, indicating potential contagion risk.
Collateral value for machinery has decreased by 10.8% from its peak value.
The Seafood industry is in a downturn with a growth rate of -6.1%.

recommended_actions.rationale: The customer has triggered 5 early-warning signals, requiring monthly monitoring per policy P-17.
Collateral value has dropped by more than 10%, necessitating a request for additional collateral or a credit limit reduction per policy P-22.
A related company is past due, requiring a review of contagion risk and repayment capacity per policy P-31.

limitations: The credit officer should verify if the negative cash flow is a temporary seasonal effect or a structural issue and confirm the current financial health of the related company An Phat Garment Co. beyond its past-due status.
